authority: Owner rulings DEC-007, DEC-011, DEC-013, DEC-016, DEC-027, DEC-030, and 2026-09-26 12:38 through 15:12 CT, including addenda A1-A9, A9b and A9c. PM decisions are marked on the rule. Lane brief WG.20.01.

AS-GLOBAL-001.norm: Every world, character, creature, item and effect cell is a multiple of the 48 px grid. 1 cell = 5 ft.

AS-GLOBAL-002.norm: DEC-011 flat 1:1. No blur, bloom, glow shader, ColorMatrix, parallax filter or alpha fade. Integer presentation scale is AS-RENDER-001. A whole-pixel depth-demo offset is AS-DEPTH-001.

AS-GLOBAL-003.norm: Alpha is binary. Brightness comes from drawn frames and ramps. Pre-drawn glow frames may composite on the additive layer in AS-GLOW-001. That is not a bloom shader.

AS-GLOBAL-004.norm: The canonical master is the 226 active S/T colours in masterPalette, plus 30 reserved slots (256 slots). uf.hex is not a second master. No shrink. Ramp ids stay the vocabulary.

AS-GLOBAL-005.norm: One light direction: top-left, 315 degree azimuth, 45 degree elevation, baked into the frames. Highlights on top and left. Shadows on bottom and right.

AS-GLOBAL-006.norm: Selout is 1 px on the outer silhouette, local ramp, darker on the bottom and right. AS-LOCK-001 locks it on characters and items. Terrain tiles have none. Depth overlays may keep one.

AS-GLOBAL-007.norm: Contact shadow is a drawn ellipse at the shadow anchor. Seamless ground tiles carry no baked cast shadow. No drop-shadow filter.

AS-GLOBAL-008.norm: Inside a layer the order is ground, strata, objects, body, equipment, effects, UI. Map order is row, then Z layer (AS-PROJ-001).

AS-GLOBAL-009.norm: Equipment draws in DEUS_Anim slot order: feet, legs, waist, armor, torso, neck, shoulders, arms, hands, ring1, ring2, head, eyes, back, offHand, shield, mainHand, weapon.

AS-GLOBAL-010.norm: Catalogue id is BAND_BIOME_CATEGORY_TYPE_VARIANT_STATE: six fields, letters and digits, hyphen inside a field.

AS-GLOBAL-011.norm: A leading $ is one character on the sheet. A leading ! is an object with no foot offset. Eight characters per sheet when the $ is absent: 4 by 2 blocks.

AS-GLOBAL-012.norm: A character or layer sheet has a sidecar of the same basename with frameWidth, frameHeight, anchor, footprint, facings, animations, frameMs.

AS-GLOBAL-013.norm: An RMMZ charset block is 3 columns by 4 rows. Walk playback is stand, left, stand, right. The walk block is never given another facing row.

AS-GLOBAL-014.norm: A face sheet is 576 by 288, eight 144 by 144 cells, 4 columns by 2 rows.

AS-GLOBAL-015.norm: SV battlers (9 by 6 motions of 64 by 64, sheet 576 by 384) are required for humanoids and for creatures Medium or larger. Tiny and Small critters have none. SV does not replace map rows.

AS-GLOBAL-016.norm: Large frames are 48 by 96 (tall) and 96 by 48 (long). Extra action rows are further $ sheets or sidecar rows. They do not break the 3 by 4 walk read.

AS-GLOBAL-017.norm: Runtime scale, rotation or tint is not a substitute for a drawn frame. AS-RENDER-001 is integer scale of the finished frame. AS-PM-001 allows an offline east-to-west mirror for bodies, gear layers and creatures. Weapons and shields are not mirrored onto the wrong hand.

AS-GLOBAL-018.norm: 32 Z layers and nine races stay. A9c replaces the layer height: 1 layer = 5 ft = 48 px, four quarters of 12 px. The 10 ft layer and five 2 ft strata are not used.

AS-GLOBAL-019.norm: DEC-030 bands and biomes are the vocabulary. Legacy catalogue band and biome tokens are not yet mapped and are unknown, not a pass.

AS-GLOBAL-020.norm: SRD 5.1 is the rules authority. V64 is retired. Presentation follows SRD conditions, damage types, sizes and spells.

AS-GLOBAL-021.norm: DEC-016: the scale chart governs drawn size. Numeric source game/data/DEUS_ScaleRegistry.json. Picture art/reference/DEUS_HUMAN_SCALE_STRIP_V1.png. Catalogue copy art/catalogue/scale_chart.json.

AS-GLOBAL-022.norm: Characters and creatures use four directions, row order South, West, East, North.

AS-GLOBAL-023.norm: A sheet that declares SW, NW, NE or SE is a legacy 8-way source. Mine S, W, E, N only. The diagonals are not standard.

AS-CRIT-001.norm: Tiny and Small creatures require idle, walk, attack, hurt and death, each in four directions.

AS-CRIT-002.norm: Fly and swim rows are optional. When declared they use the same four directions.

AS-CRIT-003.norm: A critter has a corpse sprite and a harvest icon. It has no face.

AS-CRIT-004.norm: Frame size follows the frame class and AS-SIZE-001. Tiny, Small and Medium are 48 by 48. Tall Large is 48 by 96. Long Large is 96 by 48. Huge and Gargantuan use the square, tall and long classes in sizeFrames.

AS-BEAST-001.norm: Medium and larger creatures include the critter rows plus one attack row per declared natural attack.

AS-BEAST-002.norm: Medium and larger creatures use the same 15 condition treatments as humanoids.

AS-BEAST-003.norm: Medium and larger creatures have an SV battler.

AS-BEAST-004.norm: Large, Huge and Gargantuan frames are the squares in AS-SIZE-001, authored at that size. They are not a runtime scale of a Medium frame.

AS-HUM-001.norm: Each of the nine races has a male and a female body template. Today only HUMAN male T0 and HUMAN female T0 exist in the catalogue.

AS-HUM-002.norm: Socket ids are fixed. The human 48 px stand-down baseline is recorded. Other frames store their own coordinates under the same ids.

AS-HUM-003.norm: Part layers: body, eyes, hair front, hair back, beard, and racial ears, horns, tail, scales where that race has them.

AS-HUM-004.norm: Paper-doll z-order is legs 1, torso 2, clothes 2, head 3, back 4, shield 5, held 6, fx 7.

AS-HUM-005.norm: The face shows the same armour and helmet as the charset, and no cloak or collar. Gear on a face is armour and helmet only.

AS-HUM-006.norm: Age is a visible axis. Child, adult and a stooped working elder are required. Further steps, including a teen stage, are an open Owner question.

AS-HUM-007.norm: Hair greying is a four-step ramp: natural, salt-and-pepper, grey, white. Balding is three overlays (receding, crown, advanced) that sit on any hair style. PM decision 13:02 CT, Owner may amend.

AS-HUM-008.norm: Visible genetic loci and the parts they select are defined here. Inheritance math stays in the sim.

AS-HUM-009.norm: Humanoid action rows cover the charter families, the lane list, and the A9 rows prone, unconscious, sleep and sit. Sneak and climb stay. Four directions each.

AS-HUM-010.norm: Pose families F01 through F14 map onto those rows. F14 frames for sleep, prone, unconscious and dead must be distinguishable. Whether they share one family id is open.

AS-HUM-011.norm: Emotes use the RMMZ balloon sheet: 384 by 720, 8 frames by 15 rows of 48 px.

AS-HUM-012.norm: All 15 SRD conditions have a DEC-011 treatment: pose, frame-freeze, drawn ramp, decal or icon. Invisible is a drawn contour, not a filter.

AS-HUM-013.norm: Pregnancy is a presentation hook with stages 0, 1, 2 and 3: a torso decal per race rig, not a new combat sheet.

AS-HUM-014.norm: dominantHand is right or left. Grips are ONE_HANDED, OFF_HAND, TWO_HANDED, VERSATILE. A mirror exists only under AS-MIRROR-001.

AS-HUM-015.norm: The 135 outfit ids stay as item and icon ids. Class garb is drawn in the race and class base body. Light, medium and heavy stay armour layers. Pixels stay custom per race.

AS-HUM-016.norm: PM-proposed, Owner may amend: body poses are drawn once. Garb layers match that grid. Weapons and shields pick a pre-drawn angle at a per-frame anchor. No runtime rotation.

AS-HUM-017.norm: Large shields and bows mid-draw keep per-pose frames. Capes are not drawn. Long robes are part of the class base body.

AS-HUM-018.norm: Visible body loci: height and build inside the scale-chart envelope, horns, tail, ears, and a dragonborn scale-colour ramp family.

AS-HUM-019.norm: A child body template and a stooped elder template both carry the work and action rows.

AS-FACE-001.norm: Each race has a faceset background keyed by that race ramp and motif.

AS-FACE-002.norm: Face layers stay in order. Layer 6, worn gear, is armour and helmet only. Collar and cloak are not drawn on the face.

AS-FACE-003.norm: Eight expressions in index order: neutral, happy, angry, sad, surprised, hurt, determined, afraid.

AS-FACE-004.norm: Face anchors on the 144 px cell: neck base, collar line, chin, eye line, crown.

AS-BIOME-001.norm: Six biomes times five depth bands is 30 sets, plus 15 pairwise transitions and a reserved open-air band.

AS-BIOME-002.norm: Each biome-depth set has ground, cliffs, ramps in 12 px quarters, water, vegetation, props, four seasons and a ramp id. A half-step slope is 2 quarters (24 px).

AS-BIOME-003.norm: TEMP, WET, ARID and VOLC keep the WG.00.04 physical identities under the DEC-030 ids. COLD and WILD ids are required. Their look is open. HIGH is not a biome.

AS-BIOME-004.norm: Four season states are drawn frame indices. They are not a colour LUT or a ColorMatrix.

AS-BLDG-001.norm: Every faction style uses the same piece ids: foundation, wall, wall top, roof edge, roof fill, door, window, floor, pillar, connector, furniture, workstation, plus ruined and charred states.

AS-BLDG-002.norm: The six style profiles are human_frontier, dwarf_stonehold, elf_glade, halfling_homestead, dragonborn_citadel and goblin_salvage.

AS-BLDG-003.norm: Race, culture and profile gaps are listed and not filled with new lore.

AS-BLDG-004.norm: Function, grammar and style stay separate. The 12 universal building classes are the functional catalog.

AS-ICON-001.norm: One icon grid: 32 by 32 px, 16 columns, row-major index, sheet width 512.

AS-ICON-002.norm: One icon slot for every SRD weapon, armour, shield, material, tool, spell school, condition, status, resource and job.

AS-ICON-003.norm: Rarity and quality are a border or corner mark. They are not a second drawing of the icon.

AS-ICON-004.norm: Icons share the top-left light, the 1 px selout and the palette ramps.

AS-ITEM-001.norm: An item id is race-neutral. One Plate Armor, one item id, one stat block. No Elven Plate Armor.

AS-ITEM-002.norm: Layer art key is itemId + __ + race. Missing race variant falls back to __human, then to nothing. No tint and no other race.

AS-NODE-001.norm: A resource node has full, partly harvested, depleted and regrowing states, a harvest animation, a drop sprite, and one variant per biome.

AS-ANIM-001.norm: Animation is the default. A static asset names an exception on the closed list. The clock is 150 ms.

AS-FX-001.norm: A spell is cast pose, delivery shape, damage-type impact and a sim effect. No per-spell animation.

AS-FX-002.norm: Each delivery shape is one animation with a fixed frame count on the 48 px grid.

AS-FX-003.norm: The 13 SRD damage types each have an impact animation and a ramp id. An unknown type is rejected.

AS-FX-004.norm: Lingering sim effects and concentration, buff, curse and ward auras are data on the spell row.

AS-FX-005.norm: Spell rows validate against UF_SpellVisualTable.schema.json, draft 2020-12. customPiece is a hook and is null in the examples.

AS-FX-006.norm: An effect on another Z layer is drawn in that layer at 1:1, with no blur, tint or scale. Looking down shows it.

AS-FX-007.norm: World effects cover projectile, impact, fire, water and weather, with the frame counts in the animation table.

AS-UI-001.norm: Balloons, selection rings, HP bars and lower-layer overlays are drawn frames. Window skins are AS-UI-004, not one sheet per building profile.

AS-UI-002.norm: Multi-layer selection draws the same ring on each selected unit own layer at 1:1.

AS-UI-003.norm: HP, team and status are readable without colour alone. The smallest UI glyph is 16 px. Icons stay 32 px.

AS-SUMMON-001.norm: Every derived conjure, summon, animate or create-entity spell has a slot in the summon table.

AS-SUMMON-002.norm: Each summon slot has summon-in, dismiss and a controller marker. Creatures also follow the size standard.

AS-REMAIN-001.norm: Remains cover race and creature bodies, skeletons, blood, scorch, rubble, debris, and burned, frozen and flooded tile and building variants.

AS-HAUL-001.norm: Carry is drawn. Carts exist. Stockpiles have fill levels. The old carry-not-drawn rule does not apply.

AS-VEH-001.norm: Carts, wagons, boats and siege engines exist, plus a riding pose per race in four directions.

AS-LIGHT-001.norm: Night is a precomputed ramp plus drawn lights, torch glow, window glow and lit buildings. Optional crisp tint is per-pixel or per-tile, blur stays off, and the hook defaults to off.

AS-MAP-001.norm: World map, minimap, markers and one banner per style profile are specified. No art is produced here.

AS-PROP-001.norm: Shop signs, gravestones, statues and notice boards are readable props and a named static exception.

AS-STYLE-001.norm: File names follow the class patterns. The style-bible sheet is a spec only.

AS-UI-004.norm: A signature Deus skin, a Deus Dark variant, and one window skin per race (11). RMMZ Window.png regions. Player-selectable. Opaque pixels.

AS-REL-001.norm: Holy-symbol slot per deity, plus altar, shrine, drawn magic aura, spellbook and scroll. The deity roster is open. No invented pantheon.

AS-FARM-001.norm: Crop stages sown, growing, mature and harvested. Livestock young and adult. Pens. Tamed variants.

AS-FOOD-001.norm: Food has raw and cooked states, meal and ingredient classes, table and stockpile display, and an icon.

AS-DUNG-001.norm: Underground kit: cave wall, mine support, tunnel, underground water, crystal, ruin.

AS-TRAP-001.norm: Traps and hazards: pit, spikes, pressure plate, locked door, broken door, poison gas, web, quicksand.

AS-LORE-001.norm: History visuals: historical portrait, era ruin, artifact, history-log illustration.

AS-SCENE-001.norm: Event scenes founding, coronation, disaster and war are an optional spec. They are not a required set.

AS-ZONE-001.norm: Player designation overlays: dig, build, stockpile, route, blueprint ghost. Opaque drawn hatches.

AS-MKTG-001.norm: Marketing art (game icon, store banners, logo) is a later note. It is not a required set.

AS-TAME-001.norm: Tamed variants, captured or bound poses, cages and pens. Collar, saddle and harness are visual markers only, and whether they are wanted is open.

AS-TAME-002.norm: Tamed creatures use the SRD stat block and natural attacks only. No creature armour slot, barding or crafted creature gear.

AS-VAR-001.norm: PM decision, Owner may amend. Per-biome floors: 12 trees, 4 bushes, 6 scatter, 6 rocks, 2 ore, 3 water-edge, 2 landmarks. Per underground band: 4 cave formations, 2 fungi or crystals, 1 ore.

AS-VAR-002.norm: PM decision, Owner may amend. Variety seasons are palette-swap frames on precomputed season ramps. Flip is offline and only when shading is light-neutral.

AS-GENE-001.norm: PM decision, Owner may amend. Hair, balding, facial hair and face-gene counts per race and body type. The sim owns inheritance.

AS-PORT-001.norm: Every non-face entity has a 32 px icon and a 144 px portrait. Race-neutral items have one portrait per race art variant.

AS-HEAD-001.norm: Hair, balding, beards and head race-features are 12 frames: 4 directions times 3 head states, on a per-frame head anchor. Long-hair extras only on death and dodge.

AS-ELDER-001.norm: Offsets place adult armour, helmet and hair on the elder. Elder base bodies vary by race and class (216 sheets). That count is flagged for the Owner.

AS-GEAR-001.norm: Accessories, weapons and tools are one silhouette, a race ramp and a motif decal slot. The 135 outfits stay custom per race.

AS-MIRROR-001.norm: The offline symmetric bake remains. AS-PM-001 separately allows west-from-east for bodies, gear layers and creatures, with weapons and shields on hand anchors.

AS-POSE-001.norm: Pose rows prone, unconscious, sleep, sit, sneak and climb, four directions. Prone and unconscious map to those SRD conditions. The other four are activity rows.

AS-BIOME-005.norm: A declared canonical biome set must be the six DEC-030 biomes. Five-biome registries and the catalogue canonical list fail. Those files are not edited here.

AS-SIZE-001.norm: Creature frames in 48 px squares: Tiny, Small and Medium 1x1; Large 1x2 or 2x1; Huge 3x3, 2x3 or 3x2; Gargantuan 4x4, 3x4 or 4x3. Largest action row 768 by 768.

AS-SLOT-001.norm: Source templates: charset 576x384, faces 576x288, tileset B-E 768x768, action-row strips 4 by 4 cells times the footprint. Runtime atlas 2048 with a 42 by 42 cell grid. 4096 only for terrain if benchmarked.

AS-PIPE-001.norm: No scaling. Off-size, off-palette or off-anchor output is rejected and regenerated. Crop only transparent margins. MISSING comes from empty slots.

AS-PROMPT-001.norm: Each asset category has a prompt-spec field template. Fields and sources only. No prompt is run and no image is made.

AS-GEN-001.norm: A generation log records prompt spec, generator and version, model, seed, settings, references, and pass or fail with reason codes.

AS-GEN-002.norm: Yield, cost and time per usable slot are tracked per generator, category and template, and trended over time.

AS-GEN-003.norm: Prompt templates are versioned. A version is promoted only when an A/B yield beats the current version.

AS-GEN-004.norm: Generators, per-generator adapters from one shared spec, routing by yield per cost on a fixed golden test set, and cross-generator checks. Style tune is optional and later.

AS-SRC-001.norm: The committed paper-doll example stays 768 by 1440, under the 2048 cap. A9c sheet counts and the 708-cell frame budget are AS-VIS-001 and AS-LOCK-001. They do not resize this example.

AS-REPO-001.norm: Blank template geometry and the slot map are committed as data. Approved art is Git LFS. Raw generations, rejects and logs stay out of the repo. This lane commits no pixels.

AS-PREVIEW-001.norm: Every generated asset is previewed in an animated in-game 1:1 scene and sent to the Owner for yea or nay before merge.

AS-GEN-005.norm: One generator per category. One generator id per layered set. Two or three generators once the roster is assigned. No mixing inside a paper-doll set or a creature family.

AS-SEX-001.norm: Male and female adult and elder bodies, and a child body, stay. Class garb is in the base body. Armour and helmet are drawn on adult male, adult female and the child. Elder armour and helmet reuse the adult sheet.

AS-SEX-002.norm: A creature is sexVariant none or dimorphic. Dimorphic creatures have male and female sets, each with base, tamed and saddle. A none creature has no sex set.

AS-ID-001.norm: Every slot has a permanent unique human-readable id, never reused. Runtime and packer resolve by that id only. The id matches its category grammar and links to catalogue id, sheet, cell, anchor and provenance.

AS-ANCHOR-001.norm: The tool detects landmarks and shifts the frame by whole pixels onto the slot anchor, then records the detected anchors. Clipping, wrong proportions, wrong size or head drift is rejected and regenerated. The shift is not scaling.

AS-EQUIP-001.norm: Every body frame stores main-hand and off-hand anchors, a grip angle and a draw-order flag. Down is in front. Up is behind. Weapons and shields are drawn once per grip pose and pinned by the compositor.

AS-LOOK-001.norm: Readable high-contrast fantasy. Ultima VII oblique reference. Head about 1/5 of body height. The checker tests the ratio.

AS-PROJ-001.norm: Oblique top and front. Draw order is row, then layer. Four directions. Eight directions stay declined. Diagonal movement is free.

AS-FURN-001.norm: Furniture and placeables have four facings. Symmetric reuse is by flag only.

AS-TERR-001.norm: 48 px tiles-pro Wang tiles on a dual-grid renderer. 24 px detail decals. Trial findings are recorded. 64 px tiles are not adopted.

AS-TRACK-001.norm: Ground marks: boot, bare, paw, hoof, on snow, mud, sand, blood and wet, four directions, three fade steps. A path may become a road.

AS-GLOW-001.norm: Every light-source id has a glow id with a master-palette colour and a radius, on the additive light layer.

AS-DEPTH-001.norm: Depth ramps, cliff faces, dithered shadows, ledge rims, ramps and half-steps. Depth-demo toggles are listed. Renderer code is not this lane.

AS-WITEM-001.norm: Every item has an oblique world sprite, an icon and a 144 portrait, with anchor, footprint and sim-hook fields.

AS-FEAT-001.norm: Seasonal variants, damage stages, and sim work animations on the layered humanoid system.

AS-PLAY-001.norm: Placement fields: 12/24/48 px true size, 6 px cells, quarter heights, weight, passability, and the 100,000 item benchmark.

AS-CONT-001.norm: Container art and fields: open and closed four-facing sprites, open animation, window background, SRD capacity.

AS-SCALE-001.norm: 1 Z layer = 5 ft = 48 px. Movement, light, falling, carry and the 6 second tick. 64 px tiles are not adopted.

AS-RENDER-001.norm: Integer scale only, 2x default, nearest-neighbour. Letterbox or more map. Depth demo toggles 1x, 2x and 3x.

AS-XLAYER-001.norm: Cross-layer ground collapse, 4-stage wall breaches and cave-ins, through the mass ledger.

AS-QTR-001.norm: Four quarters of 12 px replace the old strata split. The head ratio is not a quarter split.

AS-SITE-001.norm: Construction category: palette-swap ghost, blueprint, foundation, scaffolding, partial build, site props, build animation.

AS-READ-001.norm: Grayscale value step before approval. 12 px items use the stricter step. The table-with-items reference is reviewed at true 2x.

AS-PAL-001.norm: Saturated controlled palette, value first, brightest colours reserved, mood from lighting, grayscale before approval.

AS-LOCK-001.norm: LOCKED style defaults, including the 15:05 CT revision. One master, colour caps, frame budgets, additive glow, grading, 32 px icons, shape markers.

AS-MELEE-001.norm: U7 melee: separate weapon sprite, six-frame attack, swing types, hit spark, knockback, drawn 10 to 20 percent larger, not scaled.

AS-PM-001.norm: PM defaults the Owner may override: size classes, footprints, the nine race heights, doors, mirroring, fortress view, range markers, pixel font.

AS-VIS-001.norm: Visible gear is limited. Class garb is in the base body. Sheet counts are recomputed. The elder race-and-class count is flagged.

hairStyle.note: Legacy bake has 4 styles. AS-GENE-001 requires 12 per body type.

balding.status: PM decision 13:02 CT, Owner may amend

animations.note: Four states, not a loop: spring, summer, autumn, winter.
Drawn dither. Binary alpha. Not a blur.

exclude.Gate: Text: "You conjure a portal". A portal is a travel opening, not a creature or a field token.
exclude.Magnificent Mansion: Text: "You conjure an extradimensional dwelling". A place, not a creature or a field token.
exclude.Web: Text: "You conjure a mass of thick, sticky webbing" that fills a cube. Area delivery, not an entity slot.

summonDerivation.method: Include a kind:spell entry when its name starts with Conjure, Animate or Wall of, or its name is in the named list, or its description matches "you conjure" or "you summon", unless the name is in the exclude map. Exclusions are spells whose own text creates a portal, a dwelling or a cube of webbing.

summons.name: Animate Dead
summons.note: Bones become a skeleton. A corpse becomes a zombie. Text of the spell.

summons.name: Animate Objects
summons.note: Spell-defined object. Size is the animated object, Tiny through Huge. Text forbids anything larger than Huge.

summons.name: Arcane Hand
summons.note: Text: a Large hand of force. Spell-defined object, AC 20.

summons.name: Conjure Animals
summons.note: Text: fey spirits that take the form of beasts. The sim picks a beast stat block at cast. No single creature id.

summons.name: Conjure Celestial
summons.note: Text: a celestial of challenge rating 4 or lower.

summons.name: Conjure Elemental
summons.note: Text example: an elemental appropriate to air, earth, fire, or water. CR 5 or lower.

summons.name: Conjure Fey
summons.note: Text: a fey creature of CR 6 or lower, or a fey spirit in the form of a beast of CR 6 or lower.

summons.name: Conjure Minor Elementals
summons.note: Text: elementals in the listed CR options.

summons.name: Conjure Woodland Beings
summons.note: Text: fey creatures in the listed CR options.

summons.name: Create Undead
summons.note: Base text: each corpse becomes a ghoul. Higher slots name ghasts, wights, and mummies.

summons.name: Faithful Hound
summons.note: Text: a phantom watchdog. Invisible to all but the caster. Drawn for the caster with the Invisible contour rule. No sprite for others. Not an alpha filter.

summons.name: Find Familiar
summons.note: Text lists the forms. Frog (toad) uses the frog stat block. Fish (quipper) uses the quipper stat block.

summons.name: Find Steed
summons.note: Text lists warhorse, pony, camel, elk, mastiff.

summons.name: Flaming Sphere
summons.note: Text: a 5-foot-diameter sphere of fire in an unoccupied space.

summons.name: Floating Disk
summons.note: Text: a circular horizontal plane of force, 3 feet in diameter.

summons.name: Forcecage
summons.note: Text: an immobile cube-shaped prison of force, cage or box.

summons.name: Guardian of Faith
summons.note: Text: a Large spectral guardian.

summons.name: Mage Hand
summons.note: Text: a spectral, floating hand. No size word in the text. Frame is one 48 px cell.

summons.name: Phantom Steed
summons.note: Text: a Large quasi-real horselike creature.

summons.name: Planar Ally
summons.note: Text: the entity sends a celestial, an elemental, or a fiend, and the creature appears.

summons.name: Simulacrum
summons.note: Text: a duplicate that is a creature, formed from ice or snow, using the original statistics at half hit points. Sprite is the source creature plus the summon marker.

summons.name: Spirit Guardians
summons.note: Text: spirits flit around the caster to 15 feet. Aura entity on the caster, not a separate stat block.

summons.name: Spiritual Weapon
summons.note: Text: a floating spectral weapon.

summons.name: Unseen Servant
summons.note: Text: an invisible, mindless, shapeless force. Controller sees the Invisible contour. Others see no sprite.

summons.name: Wall of Fire
summons.note: Text: a wall of fire on a solid surface.

summons.name: Wall of Force
summons.note: Text: an invisible wall of force. Drawn as opaque force-ramp panels, not an alpha filter. The SRD word invisible is the rules text. The pixels are the force ramp.

summons.name: Wall of Ice
summons.note: Text: a wall of ice, dome, sphere, or panels.

summons.name: Wall of Stone
summons.note: Text: a nonmagical wall of solid stone.

summons.name: Wall of Thorns
summons.note: Text: a wall of tangled brush.

largestActionSheet.note: one Gargantuan 4x4 action row, 4 frames by 4 directions

frameLayout.note: Item 33 replaces the 3.5 frames-per-row average (30 x 3.5 x 4 = 420). The 30 rows at the locked budgets, with rows the budgets do not name left at their A9 counts, are 564 cells. Section F adds six work rows, 144 cells. A full layer design is 708 cells. The committed hair example stays 768 by 1440.

masterPalette.reconciliation: The Lanes S/T master is the single master. Its 226 colours are the active set. Thirty reserved slots bring the slot count to 256. uf.hex is a different 256-line file, 250 unique colours, six repeated lines, and zero colours in common. It is not a second master and it is not the reserved slots. The active list is not shrunk.

artManual.16: Draw readable high-contrast fantasy at the 48 px scale. Keep the Ultima VII oblique reference. A head is about 1/5 of the body height. That ratio is a proportion, not a height split.
artManual.17: Tiles and objects show a top face and a front face. Draw the map by row, then by Z layer. Sprites stay four-direction. Diagonal movement stays free.
artManual.18: Furniture and placeables have four facings. A symmetric object may reuse a view only when its symmetric flag is set.
artManual.19: Terrain is 48 px tiles-pro Wang on a dual-grid renderer. Each biome has 3 to 5 ground types in a transition chain, with 2 or 3 plain variants. Detail decals stay 24 px.
artManual.20: Ground marks cover boot, bare, paw and hoof on snow, mud, sand, blood and wet ground, in four directions, with three fade steps. A worn path may become a road.
artManual.21: Every light source has a glow id. The glow is pixel-stepped art on the additive light layer, and it stores colour and radius with that id.
artManual.22: Depth uses per-layer ramps, cliff faces, hard dithered shadows, a 1 px ledge rim, ramps and a 24 px half-step. The depth demo toggles are recorded here. The renderer is another lane.
artManual.23: Every item has an oblique world sprite beside its icon and its 144 px portrait. Placement stores an anchor, a footprint and the sim hook.
artManual.24: Near the player, items are drawn in full. Far away, the sim keeps counts and replaces them from a fixed seed. Legal drawn sizes are 12, 24 and 48 px, with no scaling.
artManual.25: A container opens a movable window of free-placed sprites. Backpack capacity in the worked example is 1 cu ft and 30 lb. Art is open and closed, four facings, plus a window background.
artManual.26: One Z layer is 5 ft and 48 px. A quarter is 1.25 ft and 12 px. Movement, light, falling, carry and the 6 second tick use that scale. A 64 px tile is not adopted.
artManual.27: The finished frame scales by an integer only. The default is 2x, nearest-neighbour. Extra space letterboxes or shows more map.
artManual.28: Cross-layer destruction covers ground collapse, wall breaches of 4 stages, and cave-ins, through the mass ledger.
artManual.29: Partial heights are quarters of 12 px. The old five-strata split is not used. The head ratio of about 1/5 stays a proportion rule.
artManual.30: Construction art is a palette-swap ghost, a blueprint, foundation, scaffolding, partial stages, site props and build animation. The ghost is not an alpha fade.
artManual.31: Characters and items must clear their ground by the grayscale value step before approval. The table-with-items trial is the reference, reviewed at true 2x. No image is generated here.
artManual.32: The palette is saturated and controlled, with no gray mush. Value carries the read. The brightest colours are reserved. Mood comes from light and grading. Every asset passes grayscale before approval.
artManual.33: Style defaults are LOCKED. The PM may revise them on trial or style-bible evidence, with notice to the Owner. The 15:05 CT revision keeps one master, caps colours, and sets the frame budgets. Re-run the cost on 708 cells, not on the 3.5 average.
artManual.34: Trial findings: request characters at size 42, animate with skeleton-v3 on create-character-v3 bodies, then propagate armour, helmet and hair. The south walk row sits 2 px low. Force a straight-on Ultima VII view. Small item world sprites remain an open test.
artManual.35: A melee weapon is a separate sprite on the hand anchors. The attack is six frames. Draw the weapon 10 to 20 percent larger in native pixels. Do not scale it.
artManual.36: These size, footprint, door, mirror, fortress, marker and font defaults are the PM defaults. The Owner may override them. West may be mirrored from east. Weapons and shields stay on the hand anchors.
artManual.37: PM assumption, Owner may amend: class garb is part of the race and class base body. Faces show armour and helmet only. Charsets show armour, helmet, weapon and shield. Other gear is an item, an icon, a portrait or a world sprite. Elder base bodies by race and class are 216 sheets.
artManual.F: Seasonal variants, building and object damage stages, and the sim work rows sit on the layered humanoid system. New work rows are farm, mine, build, craft, fish and cook, at 6 frames. Chop and carry are already rows.

pmDefaults.raceHeightNote: Halfling and gnome use 33 inside 32-34. Half-elf and tiefling use 42, the human and elf height. The Owner may override.

visibleGear.elderFlag: Elder base bodies vary by race and class: 9 races x 2 sexes x 12 classes = 216 sheets. Owner may amend.
